newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Time running out for unresolved HK issues - Chan.
newsitem.headline: Time running out for unresolved HK issues - Chan.

text.p: Time was running out for London and Beijing to reach accord on crucial unresolved issues related to Hong Kong's handover to Chinese sovereignty later this year, the territory's senior civil servant said on Thursday.

Important transitional issues including the right of abode, bilateral civil aviation links, localisation of laws and reciprocal enforcement of judgements remained to be resolved, Chief Secretary Anson Chan told a business audience.
"We are re-doubling our efforts in the hope that we can complete most of the outstanding work at the next JLG (Joint Liaison Group) meeting," Chan said.
"But we need co-operation from both sides and are acutely aware that time is running out," she added.
The next full meeting of the JLG, the Sino-British diplomatic body hammering out details of the British colony's handover to China at midnight on June 30, takes place in London next week.
Chan, who will continue in her position beyond the handover, said she believed the future Hong Kong Special Administrative Region would start life on a "reasonably good foundation."

Not only was the economy in good shape, the selection of shipping tycoon Tung Chee-hwa to be Hong Kong's future leader and Tung's selection of his top advisory and administrative teams had been well received, she said.
But she added Hong Kong people must stand united to make China's promised "One country two systems" policy work, and resist any attempts to change what must not be changed.

"The rule of law, respect for the individual, civil liberties, freedom of expression, of assembly, a level playing field, a meritocratic, politically neutral civil service...These are the values and systems which have produced the Hong Kong that we all know and love," she said.
